proposal.text:
PEP 703, "Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython," was created on 09-Jan-2023 by Sam Gross, sponsored by Łukasz Langa, has Status "Accepted," Type "Standards Track," and lists Python-Version 3.13. Its post-history dates are 09-Jan-2023 and 04-May-2023, with a separate Steering-Council acceptance resolution.

The Steering Council accepted PEP 703 with provisos: rollout must be gradual, break as little as possible, and changes that prove too disruptive must be reversible, potentially including rolling back all of PEP 703 if necessary, although such a complete rollback was considered unlikely and undesirable.

The PEP proposes adding a CPython build configuration, ``--disable-gil``, so CPython can run Python code without the global interpreter lock, together with changes required to make the interpreter thread-safe. It states that the GIL prevents multiple threads from executing Python code simultaneously and is an obstacle to efficient use of multi-core CPUs.

The motivation emphasizes scientific computing and especially AI/ML workloads, while noting that the GIL also affects other Python users. The PEP reports that the GIL hinders inter-operator and some request-level parallelism in neural-network systems, causes contention in reinforcement-learning environments, and leads users to multiprocessing, subprocesses, shared memory, sockets, or rewriting Python code in C++, with associated complexity, IPC overhead, CUDA restrictions, and reduced accessibility. It includes attributed accounts from Heinrich Kuttler, Manuel Kroiss, Paweł Jurgielewicz, Allen Goodman, Olivier Grisel, and Ralf Gommers describing GIL-related scaling and usability problems in reinforcement learning, Dose-3D hardware communication, bioinformatics/HMMER, scikit-learn/joblib/loky, NumPy, BLAS/OpenMP threading, Dask, and related PyData workflows. The PEP also argues that library workarounds for the GIL produce harder-to-use APIs, citing PyTorch's multiprocessing-based ``DataLoader`` and issues involving ``fork()``, CUDA contexts, memory use, startup cost, fork safety, serialization, oversubscription, and explicit thread-control tooling.
proposal.title: PEP 703 acceptance and proposal to make CPython's GIL optional
